independent.summary: The same escalation remains open through a third, unauthenticated door: `POST /auth/register` (public, mounted at backend/index.js:40) takes `role` straight off the body (`const assignedRole = role || 'owner'`) and writes `roles: [assignedRole]` into memberships, so anyone can self-register with `role: 'superadmin'` in ONE request — stronger than the two-request owner path this item closes. `assertAssignableRole` is not called there, contradicting its own docblock ("called by every door that writes a role") and the test header's "three doors" framing; the new suite's end-to-end test only asserts nobody became superadmin via the invite path.

triageGrades.reason: The change is entirely about role assignment/privilege escalation in the invite, role-change and invite-accept routes, so auth is plainly touched.
No credentials, tokens or key handling are changed; the only new env var is a log-level knob.
No billing, Stripe, quota or pricing code is in the diff.
Nothing in the diff deletes, overwrites or migrates data — it only adds validation that refuses writes before they happen; the cited line is the invite POST, which is not destructive.
No external integration is added or changed; the existing Resend send is only reached with a validated role string, which is not an API-surface change.
No deploy, build, CI or version config is modified — only a documented, defaulted env var added to .env.example.

summary: The local review reported nothing at all and so missed the remaining unauthenticated superadmin door in /auth/register, and it also wrongly marked the change as destructive; its other five triage calls were right.
